previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of steal syndrome presented with inability to tolerate dialysis due to severe generalized body aches. He had previously undergone banding of his left brachiocephalic AV fistula without symptom relief. After admission, he underwent ligation of the fistula to address ongoing steal syndrome. He successfully completed two full dialysis sessions post-procedure without pain. Chronic pain from diabetic neuropathy persisted, prompting consultation with palliative care and initiation of nortriptyline. Oxycodone was increased, citalopram was uptitrated, and plans were made for outpatient follow-up with neurology, palliative care, and eye specialists. He was discharged to an extended care facility on his prior dialysis regimen via tunnelled catheter with instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.

# ESRD on HD. Patient presenting with malaise and hyperkalemia 
___ his missing dialysis. EKG without any concerning changes. As

was continued on midodrine 5mg with dialysis and sevelamer 800mg

HD d/t pain associated and fatigue with the medical system as a 
whole, ultimately decided to continue on with HD, stating clear 
future-focused goals. Tolerated HD well after pain regimen 
changed, as below.

# Pain control: generalized musculoskeletal pain worse in 
setting of dialysis.  There is difficulty with pain meds in him 
given his sensitivity to them with somnolence that develops 
quickly.  Seen by palliative care service; ultimately regimen 
chagned to OxyContin 10mg QAM (NOT BID) and oxycodone 5mg 
q6h:PRN with strict holding parameters.  Home nortriptyline and 
gabapentin were continued.

sedation from narcotics, however new infection was thought 
possible given an isolated temp of 100.8, but infectious workup 
was negative, and there were no further fevers.  Lethargy 
improved after titrating down on narcotic meds.

# Diabetes Mellitus Type II:  hypoglycemia associated with low 
PO intake in the setting of insulin use, so lantus dose 
decreased to 8u qhs and SSI adjusted down.  Will need monitor PO 
intake at SNF and BGs to see if need to go back up to full dose.

with 15mg IV diltiazem; PO diltiazem was increased to 240mg
